recipes.name: Egg and Hash Brown Pie
ingredients_raw: 3 cups frozen hash brown potatoes, thawed

steps.text: Place bacon in a large, deep skillet. Cook over medium-high heat until evenly brown. Drain, crumble, and set aside.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease a 7x11-inch baking dish.
In a large bowl, beat together eggs and milk. Stir in bacon, hash browns, green onions, and 1 cup shredded Cheddar cheese. Pour into the prepared baking dish.

Bake in the preheated oven for 25 to 35 minutes, or until a knife inserted in the center comes out clean. Sprinkle remaining Cheddar cheese on top, and continue baking for 3 to 4 minutes, or until cheese is melted. Remove from the oven, and let sit 5 minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Egg and Hash Brown Pie
raw_recipe.description: A colorful breakfast casserole with hash browns and bacon, cheese, and green onions.

review.reviewBody: This recipe is wonderful, but you can take it to another level by increasing ingredients and cooking it in your crockpot over night. Increase potatoes to 32oz bag (cubed hashbrowns), 12 eggs, 3 cups shredded cheese, 1 cup milk, 1/2 cup chopped onion, 1/2 cup chopped green pepper and 1 cup or more of ham, sausage, bacon, canadian bacon, any combination you want. Cook in your slow cooker for 10 to 12 hours. You can add just about anything to this recipe and it is done when you wake up in the morning. The Smart Crockpot cooks too hot, so if using this cooker, reduce cooking time.

I'm a brunch aficienado and I found this recipe a great foundation from which one may take it in a great number of directions.
Regarding quantity - I needed to make a recipe for ~12-14 people so use a 4 Qt (8 1/2 x 14 3/4 x 2 1/4"} casserole dish. 
From the base recipe, I doubled the quantities with the following changes: 
For eggs I upped it to 12 count. every thing else doubles.
For a savory based I started by sautéing yellow onions, peppers (I used sweet peppers, but a little heat would be great, depending on your audience), mushrooms, and some cream sherry. I always like garlic , cumin and allspice . Please, use whatever tickles your fancy.
Reduce and add it to hash browns, eggs, and the other ingredients.
My bake time was 60 min. at 350 deg. I added the last topping of cheese 45 min into the bake time. I received more than a few compliments. Thanks for posting this recipe!

Cheers,
J

I doubled the recipe to use a 13x9 and let it bake a bit longer until the middle was set. Costco sells real bacon already crumbled in the bag so I dumped a bunch of that in a skillet and let it get hot. Probably about 2C. Then I put it in some paper towels and squeezed the grease out. What a timesaver!! Also - no bacon grease mess to clean up!! Came out beautiful!!

This was excellent! I did go over the reviews and proceeded with the little adjustments... Made sure to season the potato layer with some seasoning salt and melted butter in the roasting pan and pre-baked to crisp the hashbrowns before adding the egg mixture. There was so much hashbrowns for me to crisp them on the stove would've been super hard to do so I did it in a hot oven spread out in the large roasting pans and it browned nicely. I multiplied this for 32 eggs (two roasting pans) to feed a large crowd and I had many ask me for the recipe and go back for seconds and thirds... Please make sure you also season your eggs. I find that the cheese does add some saltiness but not enough so I used my extra accurate method of 2 salt shakes per egg (yes I counted out that many shakes lol) and it was perfect! Even my picky hubby loved it. We used bacon as the meat, that I cooked prior to adding to the top layer (instead of mixing in with the eggs) so it would show up nicely on the top. I reduced the amount of green onion(one bunch is maybe 1/2 cup split between the two pans) per our flavor preference and it worked out wonderfully. Baked very quickly once I added the egg mixture.

Making it the original way I found it to be kind of bland. I decided to make it again with changes. 
This time I first cooked my hash browns in a 325 degree oven on a cookie sheet til they were lightly browned. I used 1 1/2 cups of diced country ham instead of bacon and added 1/4 cup more milk to the eggs. For more flavor I also added 1/8 tsp cumin, 1/2 tsp each of garlic and onion powder and about 1/4 tsp red pepper flakes. Had much more flavor and my father said he really enjoyed it as well.

Loved this recipe! I did make a few changes. First, I cooked the hash browns for a bit and then layered the bottom of the pan with them. I did add one more egg and used 3/4 cup of milk. I then mixed the cooked bacon (cubed), cheese (Cheddar & Colby), green onions plus 1 tsp of salt, dash of pepper, oregano, garlic powder and dry mustard. Poured mixture over hash browns and baked for 20 mins. Added some more cheese on top and then let is bake some more for another 5 mins. Delicious!

I like a different version where you get the Reser FRESH shredded hash browns and press in pie pan, bake first to get toasty brown, then add Egg and other ingredients and bake. Its tastier if you do it this way.I also would put in crumbled Turkey sausage instead of bacon . Nice neat egg dish. Perfect for brunches!

Excellent base recipe! I used a lot of suggestions from other reviewers. Doubled the eggs. Oven baked the hash browns at 400 with liberal shakes of cracked pepper and the Lawrys Seasoning until browned a little. Adds quite a lot of time to prep but worth it! Used ham instead. Added a can of chopped green chiles, Mexican blend cheese (much more than called for), Lawrys seasoning to eggs too! We all loved it!

Cooked hash browns in butter and placed in the bottom of a glass pie dish. Used chopped ham instead of bacon and added a 4 ounce can of diced green chiles mixed with remaining ingredients and poured over hash browns. Wife and I loved it. Both went back for second helpings. Will make it again.

Wonderful & easy. I did cook the eggs before I baked the casserole, family isn't too much on eggs and wanted to make sure they were done, done, done! I also doubled the recipe, as I had a huge crowd for breakfast. Added cubed ham, cooked crumbled sausage and a cup of sour cream to the batch. Everyone wanted the recipe, served with hot biscuits and homemade cream gravy. Yummy!

There was no seasoning in the recipe, so I added some salt, pepper & mrs. dash garlic seasoning. Also added some fresh chopped jalapeno's and used half/half instead of regular milk, Turned out really well. Also baked it at 375.

This was an easy recipe to make. However I don’t see how this could feed 8. I made it for my family of 5 and it was all gone. In the future I would add salt. I am not one who salts my food, but this definitely needed some. I also would cook the hash browns a bit bc in some parts of the casserole they were still hard and others they were cooked. So for next time, double the recipe, add salt, cook the hash browns.
I’ll let you know after i Tri it tomorrow 😊

Made using some pineapple deli ham instead of bacon. Took other reviewer's suggestions and browned the hash browns in a skillet first according to the package instructions, and layered the baking pan; hash browns, meat/onions/cheese, egg mixture as baked as directed. Very good. The hash browns needed to have the crispness precooking them provided.
Came out delicious, did pre-cook the hash browns on the stove a bit (use the bacon grease!) and that was it.

i made this ahead of time for a long weekend getaway. Our cabin didn't have a cassarole, so I cooked it in an oiled skillet. Recipe made more than enough for two breakfasts.
I also made this recipe, but substituted some black forest ham, cut into very thin strips.
Good recipe.
I made this egg bake for Christmas morning. It was very easy to put together but had absolutely no flavor, despite adding red pepper sauteed in the bacon grease, and salt and pepper.
Very easy to make as written and family loved it. My daughter suggested adding green chili next time to change things up.
I love the ingredients, however, it was pretty flavorless. Some added spices would have jazzed it up. I ended up dumping hot sauce on it to give it some pizzaz.
